content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I would appreciate any assistance. In my temperature control project, I work with signals from two 4-20mA analog devices, and my process value (PV) is the average of these signals. I need to display both the averaged PV and the setpoint (SP) on the [product_name] operator panel. The challenge I encounter is normalizing the PV, SP, and analog output (AQ) values for proper display; my instruments have a 0 to 200°C range, which corresponds to a controller range of 0 to 1000. The problem is the PI CONTROLLER block only operates within the controller's internal scale (0 to 1000), making it impossible to directly work with normalized values (0 to 200°C). Attempts to use additional blocks for signal normalization and denormalization have not worked. If anyone can offer advice or solutions, I'd be grateful. The logic I've developed so far is provided below.

This post is closed since it was submitted twice. The other thread, titled 'PID control with averaging of two analog inputs,' is available in the relevant [product_name] software forum section. Kind regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user is seeking help implementing PID temperature control using averaged readings from two analog sensors with 4-20mA outputs. The main issue is the difficulty normalizing and displaying values in actual temperature units on the [product_name] operator panel, since the PI CONTROLLER block is limited to an internal range and does not accept values normalized to °C. Previous attempts to utilize normalization blocks were unsuccessful, highlighting workflow limitations in the current setup and potential frustration with these restrictions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants an uncomplicated way to average, normalize, and display analog input values in °C, as well as use these normalized values directly in the PI CONTROLLER and on the operator interface.
